memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Abram came to Egypt, the Egyptians saw that Sarai was a very beautiful woman. And when Pharaoh's officials saw her, they praised her to Pharaoh, and she was taken into his palace. He treated Abram well for her sake, and Abram acquired sheep and cattle... - Gen 12:14-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abram's plan works - and that is exactly the problem. Sarai is taken into Pharaoh's palace, and Abram is treated well, acquiring sheep, cattle, servants, and wealth. His compromise made him rich. On the surface, everything is going wonderfully.

This is one of the most sobering lessons in the passage: sin sometimes pays, at least at first. Abram's dishonesty produced prosperity. His fear-driven scheme brought him material blessing. If we measured success by our bank balance, Abram was thriving.

But look at the true cost. His wife - the woman through whom God's promise would come - is in another man's house. The promise itself is in jeopardy. He gained cattle and lost his integrity. He gained wealth and endangered everything that mattered.

We must be careful never to read prosperity as proof of God's approval. Wealth is not the measure of a right relationship with God. Sometimes the very thing that enriches us is the thing destroying us. Jesus asked the piercing question: "What good is it for someone to gain the whole world, and yet lose or forfeit their very self?" (Luke 9:25). Count the real cost of your compromises. What you gain may cost you far more than you know.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you measure God's approval by how well things are going?
- Is there a compromise that's paying off but costing you something precious?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, keep me from mistaking prosperity for Your approval. Show me the true cost of my compromises, and help me value integrity and Your promises above any gain.
Amen.
